application_guidance.input_pattern: A uniform finite hidden index, a common finite-volume answer space, and a common conditional density cap for every adaptive query.

sensitive_conditions: Fresh conditional sampling is required; marginal density caps do not control correlated transcript information.
The prior is uniform; no nonuniform-prior extension is claimed.
The bound counts expected queries and also covers deterministic budgets.
The transparent coordinate strengthens the Oracle only for the proof; the simulated player discards it.
K=1 is handled by impossibility, not by division by zero.

complexity_scope.guarantee: P(J=I)>=2/3 implies E[T]>=log(n)/(3 log(cV)), with the uniform hidden-index prior.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Explicit universal constant 1/3; no dependence on n, c, V or the adaptive policy.
complexity_scope.oracle: Each selected q returns a fresh observation with conditional density f_(q,I) on a common finite-volume X and common density cap c.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: One guessed index J; success metric P(J=I).
complexity_scope.regime: n>=2 and 1<cV<infinity, with almost surely finite stopping. The K=1 boundary is separately impossible at success 2/3.
complexity_scope.resource: Number T of Oracle queries in expectation. An almost-sure deterministic budget is covered as a corollary; computation is not charged or bounded.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: All measurable adaptive randomized players in the stated game, without computational or output-support restrictions beyond guessing one index.

content.intended_use: Information lower bound for guessing a uniformly hidden finite index from adaptive observations with bounded densities.

proofs.full_local_argument: This is a local replacement proof, not a quotation or a claim of independent review. Reveal the player's independent random seed to the analysis; conditional on that seed its policies are deterministic and I remains uniform. Replace every response by (x,y) uniform on G_(q,I)={(x,y):x in X, 0<=y<f_(q,I)(x)}. Each graph region has volume 1. Its x marginal is the original density, so a player that ignores y has exactly its original query, stopping and success laws. Before a query, suppose S is the set of surviving indices and m=|S|. Initially S={1,...,n}. Conditional on the full transparent history and seed, I is uniform on S: for a fixed history, each consistent index has the same product likelihood, since each transparent response has density 1 on its graph region, and the chosen queries are deterministic functions of the history visible to the player. This also holds at stopping, since the decision to stop is a function of the player's information and imposes no additional index-dependent likelihood once the full history and seed are fixed. For a chosen query define N(x,y)=sum_(i in S) 1_(G_(q,i))(x,y). The mixture response density is N/m, its support is in D=X times [0,c] of volume K, and integral_D N=m. The next survivor count is N at the sampled point and is at least 1 almost surely. With 0 log 0=0, Jensen's inequality for u log u under normalized volume on D gives integral_D N log N >= m log(m/K). Consequently E[log(m_next)|history,seed]=integral_D (N/m)log N >= log m-log K. Thus the nonnegative progress increment Delta=log m-log(m_next) has conditional mean at most L=log K. Nonnegativity follows because the survivor set only shrinks. If E[T]=infinity, the asserted bound is immediate. Otherwise T is finite almost surely. Extend the process after stopping by keeping its survivor set constant and put Delta_t=0 after stopping. The event {T>=t} is measurable before query t. Therefore E[1_(T>=t) Delta_t] <= L P(T>=t). Tonelli's theorem for nonnegative increments and the tail-sum formula yield E[log n-log m_T]=sum_(t>=1) E[1_(T>=t) Delta_t] <= L sum_(t>=1)P(T>=t)=L E[T]. At stopping, any guess based on the player's smaller transcript has conditional success at most 1/m_T when conditioned on the transparent history and seed. Hence 2/3<=P(J=I)<=E[1/m_T]. If a=P(m_T=1), the integer-valued count gives E[1/m_T]<=a+(1-a)/2, so a>=1/3. On {m_T=1}, progress log n-log m_T equals log n; on its complement it is nonnegative. Therefore E[log n-log m_T]>=a log n>=(log n)/3. Combining gives E[T]>=(log n)/(3 log K). If T<=t almost surely then E[T]<=t, proving the fixed-budget consequence. Finally, if K=1, normalization and f<=c on volume V=1/c force every f_(q,i)=c almost everywhere on X. At every adaptive query the conditional response distribution is independent of I, and the entire stopped transcript and independent seed convey no index information. Any guess then succeeds with probability at most 1/n, which is less than 2/3 for n>=2. K<1 contradicts density normalization. This completes the argument within the explicit model.

assumptions: For every q,i, integral_X f_(q,i)(x) dx=1 and 0<=f_(q,i)(x)<=c almost everywhere, with the same X and c for all queries and indices.

Conditional on the hidden index, the previous transcript and the selected query q, the next observation has density f_(q,I). This is the fresh conditional-sampling interpretation of the game; marginal density bounds alone are insufficient.
The adaptive policies and sampling kernels are measurable so that the stated conditional laws are defined. T is almost surely finite; infinite expected query count is allowed.
K>1. All logarithms use the same base; the proof below uses natural logarithms.
The total success probability, over the uniform index, observations and independent internal randomness, is at least 2/3.
statement.conclusion: Every player with success probability at least 2/3 has E[T]>=log(n)/(3 log K). In particular, if T<=t almost surely then t>=log(n)/(3 log K). The explicit constant and stopping-time statement are established by the local argument below, not quoted as printed source constants.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let n>=2 be an integer, I uniform on {1,...,n}, and X a measurable Euclidean observation region with Lebesgue volume V satisfying 0<V<infinity. For every allowed query q and index i, f_(q,i) is a measurable probability density on X. Let 0<c<infinity and K=cV. An adaptive player has internal randomness independent of I, chooses queries using its previous observations and internal randomness, stops at an integer-valued stopping time T, and outputs an index guess J measurable from that information.
statement.parameter_domains: n>=2, 0<V<infinity, 0<c<infinity, K=cV>1. Density normalization makes K<1 infeasible. At K=1 all densities coincide almost everywhere with the uniform density on X, so success for n>=2 cannot exceed 1/n; the displayed division by log K is not used there. n=1 is excluded as trivial.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every game satisfying these conditions and every such adaptive randomized player, the expected-query lower bound holds. The guarantee is average-case under the uniform hidden-index prior, not a claim of success for each index. A deterministic query budget is a special case.

summary: Density-bounded adaptive identification requires expected query count at least log(n)/(3 log(c|X|)) for success at least 2/3, under the explicit fresh conditional-sampling model and c|X|>1. A complete local replacement argument repairs the source's guessing and stopping-time gaps; independent review is pending.
title: Density-limited noisy query lower bound
use_when: Bound adaptive identification queries under a uniform finite prior and a common finite-volume observation domain with uniformly bounded conditional densities.
